highlights: Delivery work moved forward well: 2 of 3 tasks under “Stabilize MVP delivery” were completed, including stabilizing chief routing and patching the inbox acknowledgement flow.
The week showed clear recovery after disruption: prompt work was first interrupted by meetings, then successfully resumed and completed the next day.
Recovery signals improved by the end of the week, with better sleep, lower audio stress, and eased video fatigue after a shorter workday.
blockers: Recovery work lagged behind delivery work: both tasks under “Protect recovery budget” remain unfinished, with one still blocked.
Meetings and interruptions broke planned focus blocks and slowed progress during the middle of the week.
Energy was inconsistent, especially after short sleep, and fatigue stayed elevated late in the sprint.
trends: Focus started strong, dipped during interruption-heavy midweek periods, then improved again after task size was reduced and recovery increased.
Delivery execution was more reliable than recovery maintenance: shipping tasks closed, while sleep and missed-call review work remained open.
Stress markers were highest during meeting-heavy windows, while better sleep and a shorter day corresponded with more stable emotion and video signals.
nextSuggestions: Finish one recovery task early next week—either add the sleep trend check or unblock the missed call review—so recovery work stops trailing delivery work.
Keep using shorter, explicit focus blocks after meetings, since the data suggests smaller restart steps helped focus recover.
Protect sleep before heavy delivery days, because improved rest appears to correlate with lower stress and better focus stability.
